text:
sam: Weird one this morning: after installing redwoodctl on a clean Win11 machine, `redwoodctl login` immediately errors with 'spawn EACCES' if I run it from PowerShell, but from cmd.exe it works fine.

ivy: Any chance you have a PowerShell alias or function named redwoodctl? `Get-Command redwoodctl` will show. Also what's the exact error stack?

sam: `Get-Command redwoodctl` -> `CommandType: Alias Name: redwoodctl -> C:\tools\redwood\redwoodctl.exe` (we had a legacy alias created by a script). Error text when running `redwoodctl login`: `error: spawn EACCES at ChildProcess.spawn (node:internal/child_process:xxx)`. Running from cmd yields the device flow popup and completes.

lee: Alias pointing to exe path is fine normally, but PowerShell aliases don't preserve quoting for paths with spaces and can inject the alias into the child process spawn. If the alias pointed to a link that no longer exists you get EACCES. Try `Remove-Item Alias:\redwoodctl` then run `C:\Program Files\Redwood\redwoodctl.exe login`. Also check `Get-ChildItem Alias:` to find other clashing aliases.

sam: Removing the alias fixed it! But we should consider protecting against this: user mistake left an alias and the CLI failed with a low-level spawn error instead of a helpful message.

ivy: Agreed. We should detect when the resolved command is an alias or function and print a clear error: "Found PowerShell alias/function named 'redwoodctl' pointing to X; please remove it or run full path." Also consider a `--diagnose-shell` subcommand to print resolver info.

lee: Another wrinkle I saw in the logs: when the alias pointed to a symlink under `C:\Users\Sam Dev\bin\redwoodctl` (space in profile) the installer created a Start Menu shortcut that used the long path, and PowerShell resolved the alias differently. Edge case: our Windows credential helper fails when launched via an alias because the working directory is different; we should ensure path resolution uses `GetFinalPathNameByHandle` on Windows and normalize spaces.

sam: For immediate DX fix I added a `redwoodctl doctor --shell` that checks `Get-Command` on Windows and warns about aliases/functions and about non-ELF/PE mismatches on WSL. Could be useful.

ivy: Also add a user-facing fallback: if spawn returns EACCES on Windows/PowerShell, CLI should surface: "Permission or shell alias error: check PowerShell Alias (Get-Command redwoodctl), remove alias via Remove-Item Alias:\redwoodctl, or run full path." Right now it's too opaque.

sam: Filing a short repro and attaching my `Get-Command` output. Minimal repro: create alias `Set-Alias redwoodctl "C:\Users\Sam Dev\bin\redwoodctl.exe"` then run `redwoodctl login` in PowerShell, observe EACCES.

devex-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-7321: "PowerShell alias/function collision: improve error message for spawn EACCES, add doctor --shell checks, and normalize Windows path resolution for credential helper."

sam: Thanks. Also adding note to Windows install doc: avoid creating shell aliases that shadow the binary; installer will try to remove old aliases on upgrade but sometimes it misses user-created ones.

lee: Will follow up with a small PR to improve the spawn error mapping and add the doctor check. :+1:

ivy: Great catch, Sam. This will save a lot of confused Windows users.

sam: Cheers everyone. Test plan: reproduce with a few alias shapes and ensure doctor warns and error message is actionable.

devex-bot: Linked DEVEX-7321 to onboarding checklist and set P1 for the doctor improvement.
